key: Friends on that day will be foes one to another, save those who kept their duty (to Allah).
s: Between the sudden Hour and the welcome into the Garden, the surah speaks of friendship; Ibn Kathir, on 43:66 to 43:73, reads it as every friendship not for God turning to enmity at the Resurrection, while one for God lasts as He lasts.

evidence.gloss: ‘Friends on that day will be foes one to another, save those who kept their duty’: that is, every friendship and companionship for other than God turns on the Day of Resurrection into enmity, except what was for God, mighty and majestic, for that lasts as long as He lasts.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, Az-Zukhruf 43:67, at 4391). Opened Ibn Kathir on 43:66 to 43:73 (one segment) through packet.js --verse 43.67, beside al-Tabari (43:67 to 43:68), al-Qurtubi and the Jalalayn. Ibn Kathir’s own gloss (ay) on the ayah says every friendship and companionship for other than God turns into enmity on the Day of Resurrection except what was for God, which is lasting through His lasting (the pronoun most naturally refers to God, just named); he then cites Abraham’s words at 29:25 and reports from ʿAli, Ibn ʿAbbas, Mujahid and Qatada. The sentence paraphrases his gloss without drift. Plain sense: 43:66 speaks of the Hour coming suddenly and 43:68 to 43:70 of the welcome into the Garden, so the context clause is faithful and repeats no four words of the key.
